root_cause.text: `xfs_alloc_buftarg()` in XFS failed to release the DAX device reference on its error path, causing a resource leak in the `btp->bt_daxdev` lifetime management introduced by XFS DAX failure-notification support.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `fs_put_dax(btp->bt_daxdev, mp);` immediately before `kfree(btp);` in the `error_free:` path, and the commit message explicitly says “In the error path, call fs_put_dax() to drop the DAX device reference,” indicating the bug was the missing reference drop on failure.

intent_record.intent_summary: Release the DAX device reference on xfs_alloc_buftarg() failure to fix a resource leak.
intent_record.what: A call to fs_put_dax(btp->bt_daxdev, mp); was inserted in the error_free path immediately before kfree(btp); inside xfs_alloc_buftarg().
intent_record.how: If xfs_alloc_buftarg() fails after a DAX device reference has been acquired, the new call releases that DAX reference before freeing the buftarg structure, preventing a resource leak on this error path.

candidates.rationale: On the error path, the function frees the buftarg object but does not release the acquired DAX device reference associated with btp->bt_daxdev, leaving that reference leaked when xfs_alloc_buftarg() fails.

vuln_statements.explanation: This error-path free releases the buftarg object but, before the fix, did not also drop the acquired DAX device reference held in btp->bt_daxdev. That missing put caused the resource leak in xfs_alloc_buftarg() failure handling.

    xfs: convert remaining kmem_free() to kfree()
    
    The remaining callers of kmem_free() are freeing heap memory, so
    we can convert them directly to kfree() and get rid of kmem_free()
    altogether.
    
    This conversion was done with:
    
    $ for f in `git grep -l kmem_free fs/xfs`; do
    > sed -i s/kmem_free/kfree/ $f
    > done
